memos.headline: S09 and S02 Lead on Relative Strength; Most of the Universe Remains in Downtrends Below Key Averages
memos.body: I see a sharply bifurcated tape across this universe as of 2025-03-21. S09 is the standout: it is the only name trading above both its 50-day and 200-day means (+5.0% and +1.2% respectively), with RSI at 62.7, a shallow -7.9% drawdown, and dominant relative strength vs SPY of +10.3% over 4 weeks and +13.7% over 12 weeks. S02 has staged an impressive 4-week rally of +10.8% and now sits just above its 50-day mean, though it remains -5.2% below the 200-day and -17.3% off its 52-week high, so I treat this as a counter-trend bounce rather than a confirmed trend change. On the weak side, S05, S03, S10, and S08 are all deeply below both moving averages with RSIs in the high-30s to low-40s and 12-week relative strength vs SPY of -8% to -10%—classic downtrend profiles I want to avoid until price reclaims the 50-day mean. S01 is the most neutral name: only -7.2% off its high, hugging both averages, with positive relative strength, but RSI at 42 and no momentum to speak of.

views.note: Only name above both 50d and 200d means with strong relative strength; would reassess on a close below the 200d mean (~114).
Strong 4w bounce (+10.8%) and best 4w rel strength (+16.8%), but still well below 200d mean; needs to hold above 510 to stay constructive.

memos.headline: S10's 56% Net Margin and 78% Revenue Growth Stand Out; S02 and S09 Show Earnings-Power Weakness
memos.body: I see the clearest durable earnings power in S10, which posted $39.33B in revenue (+77.9% YoY) with a staggering 56.2% net margin and only $8.46B in total debt — a pristine balance sheet funding explosive growth. S05 and S04 also impress: S05 delivered $96.47B revenue (+11.8% YoY) at a 27.5% net margin with modest $14.79B debt, while S04 hit 34.6% net margin on $69.63B revenue (+12.3% YoY). On the other end, S02's 5.5% net margin on $100.81B revenue with $76.90B in debt and only +1.6% net income growth signals thin, leveraged earnings I'm unwilling to pay for, and S09's -1.1% revenue decline with a 9.1% margin and flat earnings is similarly unattractive. S07 concerns me with a -5.0% revenue decline and $31.74B debt against just $16.21B in revenue; I'd need to see a top-line inflection before getting constructive. A deterioration in S10's gross margin or a deceleration in its data-center revenue mix would change my view there.

views.note: 77.9% YoY revenue growth, 56.2% net margin, and only $8.46B debt make this the strongest earnings-power story in the universe.
Solid 27.5% net margin with +28.3% net income growth and a clean $14.79B debt load on nearly $100B revenue.
34.6% net margin and +12.3% revenue growth demonstrate durable high-margin earnings, though $44.97B debt warrants monitoring.
Revenue of $187.79B (+10.5% YoY) and an 88.3% net income jump are encouraging, but 10.7% margin and $58B debt leave limited margin of safety.
$124.3B revenue at 29.2% margin is solid but +4% top-line growth is decelerating and $94.8B debt is substantial.
32.7% net margin and +50.5% net income growth are attractive, but $401.42B total debt (financial-sector leverage) makes earnings quality harder to assess.
21.2% margin and +33.5% net income growth are decent, but only +2.1% revenue growth and $25.26B debt on $21.88B revenue limit upside conviction.
Revenue declining 1.1% YoY with a thin 9.1% margin and flat net income signals cash-flow compression risk.
Only 5.5% net margin on $100.81B revenue with $76.90B debt and +1.6% earnings growth is not durable earnings power.
Revenue down 5.0% YoY to $16.21B with $31.74B in debt — leverage is nearly 2x revenue, and top-line shrinkage is a red flag.

memos.headline: Fed on Hold at 4.50% With Sticky Inflation—Favor Defensive Sectors Over Duration-Sensitive Growth
memos.body: I see the Fed firmly in pause mode: the upper bound has been unchanged at 4.50% for three months, even as the trailing 12-month CPI print runs at 2.8% and the 3-month annualized pace (~4.0%) suggests inflation is re-accelerating. Unemployment at 4.20% is stable over three months but up 30bp year-over-year, signaling a slow labor-market softening rather than outright weakness. The 10y yield at 4.25% has fallen 27bp over three months while the 10y-2y spread has steepened to +29bp, consistent with markets pricing eventual easing but not imminent cuts. In this higher-for-longer, late-cycle regime I favor staples and banks (which benefit from a positively sloped curve and wide net interest margins) over pure duration plays and deep cyclicals; a CPI print breaking below 2.5% YoY or unemployment jumping above 4.5% would shift my call toward an easing regime favoring growth and cyclicals.

views.note: Staples benefit from a defensive tilt in a higher-for-longer, slowing-growth regime with sticky inflation.
Banks gain from a positively sloped yield curve (10y-2y at +29bp, up 61bp YoY) supporting net interest margins while rates stay elevated.
Duration-sensitive growth faces headwinds with the Fed pausing at 4.50% and sticky 2.8% YoY CPI delaying rate cuts.
Cyclicals are caught between a still-employed consumer and rising recession risk from prolonged restrictive policy; I lack conviction either way.
Energy is macro-ambiguous here—stable employment supports demand but a slowing trajectory and strong dollar from high rates cap upside.
High-beta growth names face valuation compression risk while real rates remain elevated and the Fed shows no urgency to cut.

memos.headline: Broad Negative Earnings-Season Tone Across Universe; S10 and S05 Show Deepest Post-Print Drops
memos.body: I note that every name in the universe with a Q4 earnings 8-K experienced a negative next-day price reaction, ranging from S08's mild -0.7% to S10's sharp -8.5%. This uniformly negative post-earnings tone suggests the market was disappointed across the board, but the magnitude varies meaningfully. S10 stands out with the worst reaction (-8.5%) compounded by a subsequent director departure filing on 3/7, which could signal further narrative deterioration. S05 also warrants caution: a -7.3% earnings drop was followed by a fresh Reg FD/Other Events 8-K on 3/18, suggesting the company is actively managing the narrative—either a stabilization attempt or more bad news dripping out. S08 is the relative bright spot with only -0.7% post-earnings, implying the negative tone was largely priced in or the results were close to expectations.

views.note: Worst post-earnings reaction at -8.5% plus a director departure 8-K on 3/7 signals compounding negative sentiment.
A -7.3% earnings drop followed by a fresh Reg FD filing on 3/18 suggests the negative narrative is still unfolding.
A -6.2% post-earnings reaction with no subsequent positive catalyst filing leaves sentiment firmly negative.
Only -0.7% post-earnings suggests bad news was already priced; the mildest negative reaction in the universe is a relative positive.
A -4.6% post-earnings drop is mid-range; no follow-up filings to shift the tone either way since late January.
A -2.5% post-earnings reaction is moderate and may already be digested; insufficient follow-up data to take a directional view.
Three 8-Ks in two weeks including bylaws amendments create noise but no earnings reaction data to gauge sentiment direction.
A -4.1% post-earnings drop with no subsequent positive narrative shift keeps sentiment tilted negative.

memos.headline: Policy Uncertainty Surges 154% in Three Months—Structural Risk Repricing Underway Across the Universe
memos.body: I am flagging a dramatic escalation in the policy uncertainty backdrop: the Economic Policy Uncertainty Index hit 458.66 on March 20, up 153.7% over three months and 24.7% in the last month alone. VIX has risen 26.4% over one month to 19.80, and HY OAS has widened 51 bps in a month to 3.17%, consistent with markets pricing in sustained policy-driven risk rather than a one-off shock. WTI crude at $68.55 is down nearly 6% month-over-month, which I read as demand-side concern outweighing any supply-disruption premium—suggesting the market sees trade/sanctions friction dampening global growth more than boosting commodity scarcity premia. Without specific 8-K content for S05, S06, S07, and S09, I cannot isolate company-level geopolitical exposure, but the macro regime clearly favors names with domestic revenue concentration and low supply-chain dependence on China; I would need a reversal in the EPU index below 300 or a concrete de-escalation in tariff/export-control policy to upgrade risk-on names.

views.note: Two 8-Ks in quick succession (Feb and Mar) suggest active disclosure but without content detail I cannot determine geopolitical exposure; elevated EPU warrants caution.
Three 8-Ks in ten days (late Jan–early Feb) hint at material developments, but absent content I stay neutral amid the highest policy uncertainty in years.
Single Reg FD disclosure in January provides no clear geopolitical signal; the macro uncertainty regime keeps me sidelined.
Reg FD filing in late January is stale and content-free in this dataset; with EPU at 459 I have no basis to take directional risk.
No company-specific filings in the evidence set and the 154% three-month surge in policy uncertainty argues against names with potential export-control or tariff exposure until clarity improves.
Widening HY spreads and spiking EPU create a hostile backdrop for risk; absent any offsetting geopolitical tailwind evidence I lean avoid.
